2 The objective of the Quantum Computing Certificate program is to prepare those with a degree in a STEM discipline to pivot to a job/career in quantum computing. The demand for a quantum workforce has been emphasized in the National Quantum Initiative Act (https://www.congress.gov/bill/115th-congress/house- bill/6227). For many of those who might be interested, the option of pursuing an MS or PHD is not possible because of time or expense. This certificate will present the information base to allow a person working in industry or government to advance their careers in an exciting new direction. The four courses are designed to a) refresh a background in math, with an emphasis on the language of quantum mechanics, b) establish a foundation in quantum mechanics, c) apply the foundation to the design of quantum algorithms, and d) expand the knowledge of quantum computing to the technology involved in computation, teleportation, cryptography and circuitry. July 2020 URI Online – Seed Funding Grant Proposal Program Title: Quantum Computing Department(s)/Sponsoring College(s): Physics/A&S Program Type: UG Degree Completion: # of credits: # of courses: Graduate Certificate: # of credits:12 # of courses:4 Graduate Degree: # of credits: # of courses: Intended Program Start Date: Fall’22 Contact Person: Leonard Kahn E-mail:lenkahn@uri.edu Phone:874-2053 Summary Description of Program (from URI program proposal form): This certificate program is designed for those who have a background in the STEM disciplines to develop an understanding of the the required mathematics, coding, and physics in order to interpret and develop algorithms for Quantum Computing.
The first two courses will help the students pivot to thinking in terms of quantum mechanics, where we anticipate that they have limited experience.
We build on the foundation with the next two courses, where the fundamental approaches to designing algorithms and the hurdles involved in quantum computer design will be presented.
Researchers are currently at the threshold of being able to overcome the inherent fragility of quantum computation.

At the same time advances in quantum circuitry and algorithms are being proposed that will have a significant impact on all of our lives.
Demand for a skilled workforce is a high priority from both government and industrial perspectives, because of national security the anticipated demand for services.
Major bi-partisan legislation supports increasing educational efforts to develop a quantum workforce to maintain the United States’ competitive edge.
This online certificate program complements our traditional face-to-face MS degree program, which is designed for those who will be pursuing a more rigorous training.
The proposed certificate program is targeted for those who are pursuing a career in scientific and/or engineering projects and want to broaden their background in order to take advantage of and contribute to the Quantum Computing revolution.
The four courses in the program are:

July 2020 PHY 571 (online) Math Methods for Quantum Computing: The primary goal of the course is to serve as an introduction to the mathematics that underpins quantum mechanics.
This course will serve as a refresher in linear algebra and introduce the Python computing language.
PHY 572 (online) Quantum Foundations: The primary goal of the course is to serve as an introduction to the foundations of quantum mechanics.
The distinctions between classical and quantum worlds will be described.
The quantum mechanics formalism as it applies to open systems, and its application to quantum computing will be introduced.
Special attention will be paid to entanglement and superposition.
A presentation of how qubits can be represented as vectors terminating on the surface of the Bloch sphere, how they are transformed, and the relation to unitary transformations will be made.
PHY 573 (online) Introduction to Quantum Computing: This course will introduce students to the fundamentals of quantum computing and how it differs from classical computing, including how data is stored, processed and measured.
Basic quantum algorithms will be introduced, and the question of error correction will be discussed.

PHY574 (online) Advanced Quantum Computing: This course presents applications of quantum theory to quantum computing and technology including software and hardware.
More advanced algorithms will be studied within the NISQ (noisy intermediate scale quantum) environment.
Advances in hardware design will be covered.
There will be a common theme through the courses: Students will be developing ever more complex programs using IBM’s online Qiskit, an open-source software development kit, culminating in a project in the 4th semester.
The projects will be selected in consultation with our industrial partners so that the students will be prepared for the demands of the workplace.

Summary description of proposed program (not to exceed 2 pages) The information age has brought advancements in technology and data collection techniques thatproduce an abundance of accessible data in all sectors. However, much of the ever-increasing data isunstructured and requires parsing for eﬀective decision making. Data Scientists make sense out of complex data or big data. Skills include: developing and applyingmethods to collect, record, store, analyze, and interpret data; eﬀectively extracting useful information;and detecting patterns, trends, and relationships in datasets for decision-making purposes. The data

scientist is often a storyteller presenting data insights to decision makers in a way that isunderstandable and applicable to their interests.
The ﬁeld of Data Science is interdisciplinary at its core, drawing knowledge from computer science,mathematics, statistics, and ethics, all within a framework of the domain area of the data itself.
Itsprimary goal is to gain insights and knowledge from any type of data, both structured andunstructured, and provide important resources to organizations that make data-driven decisions.Data Science is an exciting and dynamic ﬁeld that will continue to grow in importance to business,industry, science, many academic disciplines, healthcare, and government in the years ahead.
DataScientists are employed in all sectors, including ﬁnance, insurance, healthcare, social assistance, retailtrade, and manufacturing, both public and private.
Core expertise requirements for careers in data science are increasingly interdisciplinary and enabledby computational skills, requiring deep integration of data and domain subject knowledge to provideinnovative solutions to problems.

Students are exposed to an array of Data Science approachesenabling them to solve problems individually or as a part of teams.
Master of Science In Data Science Online Program Description Students learn to tackle problems that require core skills from computational, statistical, andmathematical sciences along with some domain area knowledge.
Emphasis is given tointerdisciplinary team building to solve problems that cannot be solved within a given discipline andto the ethical implications of data on individuals and society.
This program prepares data scientists toexcel in machine learning, analysis of large and/or unruly datasets, and visualization through anapproach that hones skills in problem solving and collaborative research.
In addition, studentsanalyze problems using advanced theoretical knowledge and skills of data science in statistics,machine learning theory, and mathematical methods to create innovative solutions to complexproblems in data science across a variety of domain areas.
This is a 10-course, fully online, asynchronous program that is oﬀered in the accelerated calendar ofsix 7-week sessions per year.

It is designed for working adults to take one course at a time, eachsession for 10 sessions.
Students can complete the program in 20 months.
